canonical_boundary.authority: CAPPO is the sole final consequence-authorization boundary
canonical_boundary.execution: The target adapter performs an admitted consequence
canonical_boundary.evidence: Target/native observations record outcomes but do not grant authority

required: exact source commit and dirty-worktree state captured
real service and substrate versions captured
raw stdout/stderr or API/DB responses retained
every denial has a positive control proving the test could otherwise succeed
every consequence has a before state, after state, exact target count, and correlation commitment
independent observer credentials and provenance documented
artifact manifest is signed or independently timestamped; a self-declared seal is insufficient
global_pass_gate.success: All mandatory vectors pass from one reproducible run with no synthetic fields.
global_pass_gate.kill: Any second effect, target call on CAPPO DENY, reusable terminal authority, synthetic success, missing control, or uncorrelated receipt invalidates the seal.

vectors.stimulus: Recompute hashes, verify repository commit/tree, verify signature or trusted timestamp, and mutate one byte in each artifact class.
vectors.pass: Original packet verifies; every mutation is rejected; duplicate files are counted once.
vectors.failure: Commit cannot be resolved, seal is unsigned, a mutation verifies, or an empty result is treated as evidence.

vectors.stimulus: Run one authorized create and one separately valid but policy-disallowed delete.
vectors.pass: Create causes exactly one target effect; delete causes zero target calls; both decisions and evidence bind to distinct transition IDs.
vectors.failure: Authentication, connection, attestation, or possession of a token is treated as authorization.

vectors.stimulus: Replay the exact transition and attempt a semantically identical request with changed execution metadata.
vectors.pass: Both paths cause zero additional effects after terminal success; consumed authority cannot be revived.
vectors.failure: Replay protection keys only on execution_id or client-side request labels.

vectors.claim: Real PostgreSQL schema and data compatibility
vectors.stimulus: Install schema v2 in a clean PostgreSQL instance and insert captured receipt values through the adapter role.
vectors.pass: Install and insert succeed; captured values satisfy declared types and constraints.
vectors.failure: Fixture values cannot have been produced by the declared schema.

vectors.stimulus: Observer proves one exact Tenant-B transition exists; Tenant-A login queries that transition; observer repeats the query.
vectors.pass: Worker sees zero rows while observer sees the same one row before and after.
vectors.failure: Target row existence is not proven or tenants share one session_user.

vectors.stimulus: Worker and observer each attempt INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and TRUNCATE; adapter attempts UPDATE and DELETE.
vectors.pass: Every forbidden statement fails for lack of privilege and observer proves row bytes unchanged.
vectors.failure: RLS filtering is mistaken for immutability or any application role can rewrite history.

vectors.stimulus: Worker changes custom GUCs, SET ROLE where permitted, search_path, and temp objects, then repeats PG-02.
vectors.pass: Resolved tenant remains bound to the mapped session_user; no SECURITY DEFINER object is shadowed.
vectors.failure: A pooled/shared login spans tenants or a writable schema can alter function resolution.

vectors.stimulus: Capture pg_roles, memberships, table/schema/function owners, ACLs, relrowsecurity, relforcerowsecurity, and active session_user/current_user.
vectors.pass: Worker, adapter, and observer are not superusers, do not have BYPASSRLS, do not own evidence objects, and have no path to owner membership.
vectors.failure: Any application principal can bypass RLS or assume an incompatible role.

vectors.stimulus: Inject failure after business DML and before receipt INSERT, then run the successful path in one transaction.
vectors.pass: Failure leaves neither effect nor receipt; success exposes both with one target transaction ID and matching commitments.
vectors.failure: Business state can commit without its receipt or receipt can exist without the claimed effect.

vectors.stimulus: Define canonical row serialization, hash captured before/after bytes, and mutate each committed field independently.
vectors.pass: Independent recomputation matches; every semantic mutation changes the commitment.
vectors.failure: Digest is a fixture constant, hashes empty input, or serialization is ambiguous.

vectors.stimulus: Bind admission request facts, then substitute or recreate the workload after persistence.
vectors.pass: Evidence distinguishes AdmissionReview UID from object UID and binds Pod UID, node, runtime ID, image digest, SVID, PID/starttime, namespaces, and cgroup ID before dispatch.
vectors.failure: A client-authored Pod UID or human-readable name is accepted as runtime identity.

vectors.stimulus: Read memory.max, attempt unauthorized limit modification from the workload, then exceed the unchanged ceiling.
vectors.pass: Limit mutation is denied; memory.max remains exact; memory.events oom_kill increments; runtime reports the native exit status.
vectors.failure: Only an allocation OOM is shown and labeled as a widening attack.

vectors.stimulus: Capture attached BPF program/link/map IDs and cgroup, test denied destination, allowed control destination, detach/replace attempt, and recovery.
vectors.pass: Native counters prove deny-control-recovery causality and the actual attach hook matches the claimed mechanism.
vectors.failure: Only an application exception string is captured or the named hook cannot enforce the claimed flow.

vectors.stimulus: Commit the target transaction and deterministically cut acknowledgement before CAPPO records success.
vectors.pass: CAPPO records OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, performs no blind redispatch, observer resolves the same transition, and total target effect count remains one.
vectors.failure: The test crashes before commit, does not prove dispatch occurred, or relies on executor narration.

vectors.stimulus: For each exact AWS/GCP API operation, exercise documented token scope, same-token/same-parameters, changed parameters, region/zone boundary, expiry, and unsupported-operation behavior.
vectors.pass: Veklom policy matches each provider operation's measured semantics; unsupported APIs remain fenced by Veklom transition identity.
vectors.failure: A universal ClientRequestToken/requestId guarantee is inferred across EC2, IAM, or Resource Manager.

vectors.stimulus: Correlate provider request ID, audit event, and direct resource-state readback under delayed, missing, duplicated, and out-of-order audit delivery.
vectors.pass: Success requires the operation-specific evidence profile; audit absence alone never proves non-occurrence.
vectors.failure: A status label or an audit event alone is treated as universal resource finality.

vectors.stimulus: Capture raw COSE_Sign1 document from a non-debug enclave; validate certificate chain, signature, freshness/nonce, module ID, SHA-384 PCRs, and allowlisted image measurements.
vectors.pass: Independent verifier accepts the original and rejects wrong nonce, expired/untrusted chain, debug-zero PCRs, altered PCR, and replay.
vectors.failure: A short PCR string or simulator assertion is accepted as hardware evidence.

vectors.stimulus: Run separate Nitro and AMD SEV-SNP verifier profiles with native evidence formats and roots.
vectors.pass: Each profile validates only its own evidence and maps measurements to an explicit policy consumed by CAPPO.
vectors.failure: Nitro PCR/KMS language is used as proof of SEV-SNP or attestation itself mints consequence authority.

decision_unlocked: A passing run permits MEASURED/VALID claims only for the exact commit, substrate versions, operations, and evidence profiles tested; it does not establish universal cloud, Kubernetes, database, or confidential-computing certification.
